# SBL crosswalk — the per-LO ledger

**138 rows, 138 verdicts, no gaps.** Generated by
`scripts/authoring/build-sbl-crosswalk-ledger.ts`, which refuses to write this file if a
parsed outcome has no verdict or a verdict names an outcome the study guide does not contain.
Every tally, percentage and sensitivity figure below is computed, not asserted.

Sources: `SBL-GUIDE` §5 detailed study guide pp.9-17 — LO codes, sub-area names, outcome text
and intellectual levels are a machine parse, not a transcription (92 at [3], 46 at [2], zero
at [1]). Assets are live `acca_drills` and `acca_cases` rows.

---

## Why this file exists

A previous pass produced a single headline — **35% covered** — from eight section subtotals.
The 138 individual judgements behind it were never written down, so the number could not be
re-opened at the row you disagreed with. A blind re-verdict of a random 15 outcomes came out at
**53%** against an implied 38%, and tightening the (unstated) definition of ADAPT moved that
same sample to roughly **17%**. A number whose defensible range is 17-53% is not a plan.

Two things fix that, and both are below: a **stated threshold**, and **one row per outcome** —
including a named NEAREST asset for the rows that FAILED, so moving the threshold is a re-read
of one column rather than a re-derivation of the whole exercise.

## The ADAPT threshold — stated, so it can be argued with

**REUSE** — the existing asset can be served to an SBL candidate with **no change to its
rubric or model answer**. Only the paper label changes.

**ADAPT** — a **named** asset exists whose marked act transfers, and the rewrite is confined
to re-pointing the frame. All three of the following must hold:

- **(a) OBJECT** — the candidate operates on the same kind of thing.
- **(b) OUTPUT** — the candidate must produce the same kind of output (a computed figure plus
  a verdict; a recommendation; a description; a critique). *Same model, different output, is
  not an ADAPT* — "evaluate how SWOT assists performance management" and "formulate a SWOT"
  are different marked acts.
- **(c) CONTENT SURVIVES** — the technical knowledge the rubric awards marks for is knowledge
  SBL also examines. If the rewrite has to replace what the candidate must KNOW, you are
  re-teaching, not re-pointing.

**NEW** — everything else. Three named failure modes, so each NEW records which tooth bit:

| code | the rule | why it is a rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **T1** | An asset is a **published drill, or a published case requirement on a case that is NOT `mock_only`** — never a framework LO. | APM B3e *is* Business Process Re-engineering and has **zero** published drills. Counting it would credit content that does not exist. **Reserved exam content is excluded on the same principle:** a `mock_only` requirement teaches nobody anything until it is sat, and spending it on another paper consumes the mock. That is a standing property of reserved content, not a judgement about SBL. |
| **T2** | The marked act must transfer (a/b/c above). | Otherwise "same model" silently becomes "same drill", which is where 35% came from. |
| **T3** | **One asset, one claim.** A single drill backs at most one SBL outcome. | A drill can only be rewritten once. The prior pass named one A1e drill for two SBL outcomes and one D1a drill for two more; there is one of each in existence. |

Where an outcome fails on more than one tooth, both are recorded (`T2/T3`).

## The count

| verdict | rows | share |
| --- | --- | --- |
| REUSE | 0 | 0.0% |
| ADAPT | 35 | 25.4% |
| **covered (REUSE + ADAPT)** | **35** | **25.4%** |
| NEW | 103 | 74.6% |
| total | 138 | 100% |

**25.4% covered, 35 of 138.** Not 35%.

**REUSE is zero, and that is a finding, not an omission.** No SBL outcome can be served by an
existing asset unchanged — every SBL outcome sits in a different frame (governance, the public
interest, strategy) from the performance-management and corporate-finance frames the corpus was
written in. A prior pass recorded 4 REUSE while also stating the rule "same model, different
verb, different marked act — every one of these is ADAPT, NEVER REUSE". Those four contradicted
its own law.

| section | LOs | covered | rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A Leadership | 12 | 0 | 0.0% |
| B Governance and sustainability | 27 | 7 | 25.9% |
| C Strategy | 22 | 2 | 9.1% |

| G Finance in planning and decision-making | 10 | 6 | 60.0% |
| H Enabling success, managing change and innovation | 23 | 6 | 26.1% |

The distribution matters more than the headline. Coverage is **concentrated in two sections** —
E (technology and data analytics) and G (finance), which are 27 outcomes at
**66.7%** between them, holding 18 of the 35 ADAPTs — and is near-zero in the four
sections that carry most of the paper: **A, C, D and F together are 61 outcomes at
6.6%** (4 covered). Section A is 0 of 12; sub-area F2 (audit) is 0 of 4.
A build plan that reads the headline as "a quarter of the work is done" would be wrong about
61 of the 138 outcomes.

### Which corpus pays

| corpus | ADAPTs it backs |
| --- | --- |
| APM | 29 |
| AFM | 6 |

**The first pass never considered AFM at all** — it opened on "APM 91 published drills" and
stopped there. The 6 AFM-backed rows (B2b, G2b, G2c, G2d, G2e, H6d) would all have scored NEW on an
APM-only baseline, so an APM-only crosswalk reads 21.0% and understates coverage by
4.3%. Four of the six sit in section G, which is why G is one of the two best-covered
sections in the paper and was previously read as one of the worst.

### Why the NEWs are NEW

| failure | rows |
| --- | --- |
| `T1` | 61 |
| `T2` | 30 |
| `T2/T3` | 8 |
| `T3` | 4 |

**T1 dominates, and that is the load-bearing fact for a build plan.** The commonest reason an
SBL outcome is uncovered is not that the nearest asset is a poor fit — it is that there is no
asset at all. Governance (B3, B5), audit (F2), the resource-based view (C4), project management
(H6) and most of the models SBL names by name (Johnson Scholes and Whittington, Porter's
Diamond, POPIT, Baldrige, Harmon, Lewin, Balogun and Hope Hailey, Ansoff, TARA, ALARP, COSO,
the six capitals, ICGN) appear nowhere in either corpus. **That work does not get cheaper by
choosing a looser threshold.**

## What moves the number, and by how much

The threshold is a choice, so here is its sensitivity — measured on this ledger, not estimated:

- **Drop T3 (let one drill back many outcomes).** 4 rows fail on T3 ALONE
  (C3d, D1e, E1c, E4b) and would become ADAPTs, taking coverage to
  **28.3%**. A further 8 fail on T3 together with T2.
  ⚠️ T3 is what stops the corpus being counted twice: **22 of the 35 ADAPTs rest on an asset
  with exactly ONE published drill**, so dropping T3 credits the same drill repeatedly.
- **Drop T2's output test (b) — "same model is enough".** The single APM A1e drill (SWOT, PEST,
  generic strategies) is the nearest asset for **four** outcomes (C2a, C2c, C3e, C4d), and the
  single D1a drill for four more (E1a claims it; E1b, E1c, E4b and G1a lose it). This is where
  the prior 53% came from.
- **Tighten to REUSE only.** 0%.

The 17-53% range is now a 25.4% point estimate with a stated rule and named levers, and every
row below can be argued individually.

## Reading the ledger

`asset / nearest` names a **published** asset as `PAPER LO (n)`, where `n` is the live drill
count for that LO. On a NEW row it is the nearest thing that exists, and the row says why it
was not enough; `—` means nothing in either corpus is close. **An ADAPT with no named asset is
a NEW** — that is the whole point of the column.

## The inverse finding: what the corpus holds that SBL cannot use

The ledger reads one way by design — SBL outcome → asset. Read the other way it is starker.

As at **2026-08-18** there are **154 live drills** (APM 91, AFM 63) and
**23 eligible case requirements** (APM 11, AFM 12) across the two papers —
a published asset pool of **177**. A further **15** case requirements sit on `mock_only` cases and are
NOT assets under T1. This ledger claims
**35** of the 177, one per ADAPT. **142 published assets back no SBL outcome at all.**

⚠️ These corpus figures are a **declared snapshot, not a live query** — this script reads the
study guide PDF and never touches the database, so they are judged, not derived. Re-verify with
`npm run build:sbl-ledger -- --verify-corpus` (needs `--env-file=.env.local`).

Three concentrations are worth naming:

- **APM A3b holds 9 drills** — the deepest single asset in either corpus — and backs exactly
  one SBL outcome (G2f).
- **APM C1 holds 13 drills** (C1a 3 · C1b 2 · C1c 3 · C1d 2 · C1e 3) and backs exactly one
  (B4a). Three published cases are C1-anchored — Orlen Cinemas, Aldermere Fitness and the
  reserved Rivenor Pharma Distribution — and SBL has no technical home for management-report
  quality, data visualisation or misleading presentation.
- **AFM sections C and D are entirely undrilled** (M&A, valuation of acquisitions, financial
  reconstruction, unbundling — 0 published drills across ~24 framework outcomes), so SBL C5f
  ("business combinations, strategic alliances and partnering") has no asset even though a
  well-fitting AFM framework outcome exists.

## Two things this ledger does NOT settle

1. **Outcomes, not marks.** Every row is one outcome counted once. SBL examines these
   outcomes across three tasks in one 100-mark paper, so they are not equally weighted and a
   coverage rate by outcome is not a coverage rate by marks. Weighting needs sitting-by-sitting
   evidence from `SBL-E1`..`SBL-E7`, of which **four pages of one report have been read**.
2. **An ADAPT is not a small job.** It means a named drill exists whose marked act transfers —
   not that the rewrite is quick. Every ADAPT still needs new scenario prose, a new rubric under
   the FIVE-skill vocabulary SBL uses (Analysis and Evaluation are separate skills there, and
   Enquire and Estimate have no counterpart in the four-skill papers), and a fresh pass through
   the gate barrier.
